author: tbolt
description:
A local-first recipe box. Import recipes from websites, handwritten cards, PDFs or pasted text with OpenRouter AI, then plan meals, build shopping lists, cook step by step, and keep encrypted backups.

Recipes live in your browser first; the bundled sync server keeps a copy on this disk with the last 20 versions, so a bad merge can be undone. Add an API key in Settings to enable AI import. Nothing leaves your network unless you configure sync or ask the AI to read a page.

tips.before_install:
## Recipe Box

Data (recipes, shopping lists, sync history) is stored on your ZimaOS disk at `/DATA/AppData/$AppID/`, so it survives container rebuilds.

Open **Settings** in the app to add an OpenRouter API key if you want AI import from websites, photos, PDFs or pasted text. Without a key everything else still works: manual recipes, meal planning, shopping lists, and local backups.

If this instance is reachable from other devices, set `RECIPEBOX_TOKEN` in the app's Sync dialog so the server requires a bearer token.

title: Recipe Box
release_note:
- Website import now fetches through the Recipe Box server first, from your
  own network, so sites that block public relays (Allrecipes and other
  CDN-fronted sites) load instead of failing with 503/402. The server
  route speaks HTTP/2, which those CDNs require.
- If every route fails, the import message now says whether the server
  route was tried, so the next step is clear.
- The API token now protects only /api/*, so setting RECIPEBOX_TOKEN no
  longer locks you out of the app itself.
